data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump sidelines Vance from Iran talks, says no need to negotiate
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Trump sidelines Vance from Iran talks, says no need to negotiate
President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US is no longer interested in negotiations with Iran, as he appeared to sideline his own vice president, JD Vance, who has tried to position himself as a mediator in the war.
“We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed…We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on social media, referring to the Hormuz waterway.
Trump’s statement is a flip-flop of his comments earlier this week saying that there was “momentum” for a political settlement with Iran and that negotiations were ongoing.
He appeared to relegate Vance to handling a new domestic file of what he called the “corrupt disasters” of Democrat-run cities and states.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Pro-Palestinian group seeks ban on Israeli real estate fair in Paris
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Pro-Palestinian group seeks ban on Israeli real estate fair in Paris
Pro-Palestinian activists have asked a French court to ban an Israeli real estate fair in Paris marketing Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem, AFP reported on Thursday.
The Franco-Palestinian NIDAL association filed an emergency motion with a court against the 9th Icube real estate and investment salon, arguing that the fair violates human rights.
The event is scheduled for Sunday at the European Centre for Judaism in the French capital. Other major cities have seen similar uproars over Israeli real estate fairs.
NIDAL asked the court to either order the head of the Paris police force to ban the event outright or to ensure that the event does not sell property in the West Bank and East Jerusalem, whose occupation by Israel since 1967 is considered illegal under international law.
Before taking legal action, the group said they had sent a letter to the Paris police on 5 November, which went unanswered.
In the filing, seen by AFP, the rights group says that marketing Israeli settlements in the occupied territories contributes to the forced displacement of the Palestinian people through population transfer - a practice prohibited by international law and classified as a war crime under the French penal code.
In particular, the activists highlighted that BH Nadlan, a company that markets settlements in both East Jerusalem and the West Bank on its website, will be present at the fair.
They also pointed to the fair's official guide's offer of a "significant" financial "bonus" for newcomers settling in "Judea and Samaria", the Israeli term for the occupied West Bank.

Father Issa Thaljieh, the Palestinian parish priest at the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, in the occupied West Bank, has been denied a US visa to speak alongside American clergy next week on the gravity of Israeli settler attacks on Palestinian villages.
"Our government denied him a visa for 'security reasons'. A parish priest from Bethlehem, treated as a threat. That should worry all of us, because it means the people living through this are being kept from telling us about it," Laila Mokhiber, a volunteer with Orthodox Christians for Palestine (OCP), told Middle East Eye on Thursday.
MEE has reached out to the State Department.
Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant leaders are set to gather at the United Methodist Building near the US Capitol on Monday to demand that Congress hold accountable both settlers and the Israeli military, and also curb US weapons transfers to Israel.

data.title: Middle East Eye: How Gaza’s winter ‘crisis’ is manufactured by Israel
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
How Gaza’s winter ‘crisis’ is manufactured by Israel
For the fourth winter in a row, rains have swept through Gaza, exposing woefully inadequate supplies of materials for shelter entering the strip.
This has forced 65 percent of the population - around 1.4m people - to shelter in makeshift shelters or tents which have been swamped in the downpour, or damaged buildings which risk collapse.
While the weather is turbocharged by a strengthening El Nino event, the paucity of aid is entirely man-made, leveraged as a pressure point by Israel over Gaza’s population.
The Israeli authorities have long restricted the entry of shelter and construction materials into Gaza, with vital equipment like tent poles and mobile homes deemed to be “dual use”.

Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said in an interview with Al Jazeera that Tehran has no desire to continue the war with the US, but that the ball is in Washington’s court for peace talks.
Ghalibaf said that Iran provided the US with a clear and transparent response outlining its demands, but the Trump administration has not yet responded.
An agreement with Washington is possible, he added, provided it adheres to what was previously agreed upon and refrains from actions that undermine trust and excessive demands.
He said that Iran is determined to move beyond the state of “no war, no peace” through negotiations or sustainable deterrence, and accused Washington of imposing a siege on the country by blocking access to food and hindering trade and healthcare services.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Is Saudi Arabia expanding its ballistic missile programme?
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Is Saudi Arabia expanding its ballistic missile programme?
Saudi Arabia is believed to be expanding its Chinese-designed ballistic missile arsenal as it faces an unprecedented barrage of missile and drone attacks from Yemen's Houthi forces.
Satellite imagery analysed by American researchers suggests the kingdom is expanding its ballistic missile plant at al-Duwadimi in Riyadh Province to build larger solid-fuel missiles capable of carrying heavier payloads across greater distances.
Fighting between the kingdom and the Iran-aligned Yemeni group has intensified since July, shattering a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022.
The Houthis have stepped up missile and drone attacks on Saudi cities, airports and energy infrastructure, retaliating for what they call a Saudi "blockade" of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen.
Analysts have told Middle East Eye that the renewed confrontation with the Houthis has given the kingdom's arsenal added significance.

data.title: Middle East Eye: How Israel's war on Lebanon's water has become existential
data.author: Zaynab Mayladan
data.summary:
How Israel's war on Lebanon's water has become existential
Submitted by
Zaynab Mayladan
on
Mon, 11/02/2026 - 19:08
Across the country's south, where water infrastructure has been targeted for decades, the ongoing conflict raises a key question: can life here ever get back to normal?
Insaf Faour and her granddaughter, Fatima, are pictured in August 2026 at their home in Debaal, Lebanon, which has been hit hard in Israel’s war (MEE/Zaynab Mayladan)
Off
It was half past five in the afternoon when Bahij Abdallah saw a white object pass overhead.
He was outside a pumping station in Ebel el-Saqi, in the hills above Marjayoun, checking on an open water reservoir. He had sat down on a stone step with his phone in his hand, while three colleagues remained inside.
At first, he thought the white thing was a drone.
“Suddenly, it stopped in the air for a second, turned, and fell on the station,” Abdallah told Middle East Eye. “Then the smoke and the fire started.”
The phone flew out of his hand. He felt a wall of air, and then metal pushing into his body. He looked down and saw blood dripping from his face. His shoulder was burning. When he stood up, he saw that his shoe had been cut open.
Abdallah, an electrical maintenance employee with the South Lebanon Water Establishment (SLWE), the state utility that supplies drinking water to two governorates, had been doing what he does most days: running the station and monitoring it.
The facility is well known in the region and clearly marked, he said. “There are signs, and vehicles with the name and logo on them, that it belongs to the South Lebanon Water Establishment, which is a government body. And we were wearing the work uniform.”
The attack occurred on 9 June 2026, five days after Israel and the Lebanese government announced in Washington that they had agreed to a ceasefire.
'I could have died in seconds. And I wasn't doing anything wrong; I was only pumping water for people to drink'
- Bahij Abdallah, state utility worker

data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Watch: 53 nations and organisations urge Israel to allow aid into Gaza
Fifty-three nations and organisations urged Israel on Thursday to allow urgent aid and unimpeded humanitarian access into Gaza.
Speaking on behalf of the co-signatories of the Gaza Call to Action on Humanitarian Access and Health, Sarah MacIntosh, British ambassador to the UN, also called on Israel’s incoming government to facilitate the much-needed humanitarian access into the besieged enclave.

Trump says 'not sure' if he agrees with Gulf allies on holding off on Iran attacks
US President Donald Trump said that allies from Gulf countries have requested that he hold off on large-scale attacks against Iran.
"Saudi Arabia has asked me to please just let it be the way it is now for a while," Trump said during an interview with Stephen A Smith, adding that the UAE, Qatar and Kuwait prefer the same approach.
"I’m not sure I agree with it," he said

data.title: Middle East Eye: IRGC Navy says tanker explodes after hitting a sea mine in Hormuz Strait
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
IRGC Navy says tanker explodes after hitting a sea mine in Hormuz Strait
The IRGC Navy says a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) carrier exploded after it hit a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz.
"This ship did not learn from the fate of previous exploded tankers and chose to pass with the support of American fighter jets," the IRGC said.
"Unaware that naval mines never coordinate with the American army of smugglers and aggressors to hunt their prey, it suffered a very severe explosion."
The IRGC further warned that any vessels entering "unauthorised and dangerous routes" against Iran's warnings will "suffer the same fate as the previous vessels".
